items.title: Committed execution metadata before the runner

body.Spec said: The run-plan driver owns commits between implementation phases.
body.What I did: Created one local setup commit containing the approved plan, governed workstream state, and empty implementation-notes artifact before starting the driver.
body.Why: The driver refuses a dirty tree, while the notes protocol requires the decision artifact to exist before implementation starts. No application code is included in this setup commit.
body.Risk: The branch has one metadata-only commit before the phase commits.

items.title: Ran Rails verification in the devcontainer

body.Spec said: Run the repository's focused tests and Ruby style checks before accepting the phase.
body.What I did: Ran migrations, focused Rails tests, and RuboCop inside the repository devcontainer.
body.Why: The host shell has macOS Ruby 2.6 and does not have the repository's required Bundler 2.6.7. The devcontainer provides the supported application toolchain.
body.Risk: Local verification depends on Docker being available; the same checks should also run in CI.

items.title: Hardened lifecycle boundaries after independent review

body.Spec said: Completed runs are immutable and every valid run has a rerunnable saved scope.
body.What I did: Blocked direct destruction of completed runs, required pending status on creation, validated the canonical scope shape, converted malformed legacy reruns into a domain error, and allowed the planned optional data_version field.
body.Why: A read-only review reproduced three lifecycle holes and then caught an exact-key validation rule that would have blocked Phase 2. The corrected patch passed the final review gate.
body.Risk: ActiveRecord delete and raw SQL bypass model callbacks; preventing those internal code paths would require a database trigger.

items.title: Fail closed when saved calculation inputs drift

body.Spec said: A saved run records a stable scope and data-version key, while the app owns all filtering and calculations.
body.What I did: Included live transaction, entry, account-label, category, merchant, family-currency, and relevant exchange-rate dependencies in the scope hash. Each calculation rechecks account visibility and rejects a stale data version before reading rows.
body.Why: Independent review reproduced both a post-construction authorization gap and a case where an exchange-rate edit changed totals without changing the saved scope version.
body.Risk: Computing the version currently materializes the scoped transaction history and associations; large all-history scopes need performance measurement later.

items.title: Matched Sure's transfer and account-breakdown semantics

body.Spec said: Calculations preserve Sure's existing transaction and currency conventions and expose only user-friendly account labels.
body.What I did: Excluded funds movements and credit-card payments by default while retaining loan payments and investment contributions as expenses. Account breakdowns group by internal identity but serialize only the saved label, so duplicate account names stay separate without leaking IDs.
body.Why: The first implementation treated every transfer kind alike and merged different accounts that shared a name.
body.Risk: Two same-named accounts render as separate rows with identical labels; the UI may later need a privacy-safe disambiguator.

items.title: Enforced evidence capacity under the parent-run lock

body.Spec said: Each run stores at most 25 safe evidence snapshots.
body.What I did: Rechecked capacity while holding the parent-run row lock for both new evidence and reassignment, including writes that bypass validations.
body.Why: Validation-only counting had a concurrent-insert race, and the first locked fix still allowed an existing row to be moved into a full run.
body.Risk: The regression suite proves the race windows deterministically rather than with timing-sensitive multi-thread tests.

body.Spec said: An independent read-only reviewer checks each phase before acceptance.
body.What I did: Ran three review passes, fixed every verified high- and medium-severity finding, and accepted the phase only after a clean PASS with 33 focused tests and 152 assertions.
body.Why: The review probes found authorization, stale-input, transfer-semantics, duplicate-label, and evidence-cap edge cases that the initial suite missed.
body.Risk: The full application and system suites remain deferred to Phase 5 as planned.
